pairs.difference: A: the upper arm goes near-white while the lower arm drops into the same light grey as the pale background stripe, so its edge is lost. A speckled white ring of glow sits on the floor around the base, and the darks are split between the joints and the plinth. B: the binoculars hold one big dark mass of barrels, eyecups and cast shadow on a mid-light floor, with hero-against-background separation by value. B's gap (-0.277) and rms (0.200) sit just past the real range, so this call rests on A's scattered grouping and floor glow, not the numbers.
pairs.fix: Put the arm's left side and underside in one continuous soft shadow so it stands darker than the background stripes. Remove the bright glowing patch on the floor around the base and let the floor fall off smoothly into one soft cast shadow.

Its vignette of 0.162 is high, but the grouping reads like the real glove card.
pairs.fix: Light the tanks from one side only: a soft, wide highlight on the left tank and the right tank falling into one shared shadow. Drop the repeated white stripes and lift the purple background a little brighter.

Only thin white lines outline it, the liquid is a single mid band, and there are no dark accents other than the shelf edge. A: the dark uppers and laces of the shoes and a broad cast shadow sit against a white floor, giving a strong hero-versus-background value gap, though its mean of 0.762 is also a little high.

pattern: Generated cards break the card into many small, evenly distributed light and dark pieces rather than a few large groups: repeated hard highlights, hero faces that flatten to near-white with an abrupt dark crescent instead of a roll-off, and ragged halos hugging the outline. Real cards keep one broad shadow side on the hero and a wide, gentle glow behind it. The other tell is hero separation by hue alone, where hero and background land on the same grey (bracelet, tube, flask), or the opposite extreme of near-white on near-black (tape machine).
